newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to carry forward reforms.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to carry forward reforms.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday dismissed fears that opposition agitation could destabilise her government and torpedo its reform agenda.
"They might try to create some problems but they won't succeed," she told a news conference.

"People want peace and prosperity, and my government is determined to let them have those. I am not suffering from fear or hesitation," Hasina said while briefing reporters on her recent visit to the United States.

A World Bank report last week cautioned that the previous government headed by Begum Khaleda Zia was not reconciled to its election defeat and might resort to street politics to destabilise the government and its reform plans.
Khaleda's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) lost to Hasina's Awami League in elections last June.
Hasina hit back at BNP criticism that she had compromised the country's sovereignty in making a deal with India to jointly fight insurgency along their common border.
"These sort of utterings are absolutely nonsense. Then they (opposition) don't want a solution to the insurgency problem in (Bangladesh's) Chittagong Hill Tracts," she said.

Hasina and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda last month agreed to fight insurgency jointly, a major move after the two countries had signed a 30-year treaty for sharing water from the Ganges river.
